description: Attestation vectors: every case of the attestation parity fixture that the format can express, one batch and one single request per tamper kind, policy epoch changes at request and execute, and the attester key form.

vectors.description: A valid attestation for an untagged destination is accepted, the payout expires at valid_until, and it executes.
A valid attestation for a destination with tag 7 is accepted and the payout pays the tagged destination.
A valid attestation for tag 0, which is distinct from no tag, is accepted.
A valid attestation for the largest u64 tag is accepted.
A valid attestation for a contract destination is accepted.
Two legs to one address under tags 1 and 2, each with its own attestation, are accepted.
An attestation valid for exactly MAX_ATTESTATION_VALIDITY from now is accepted.
An attestation used one second before valid_until is accepted, and the payout expires at valid_until.
After three policy changes an attestation issued under policy epoch 3 is accepted.
The amount is not attested: a payout of 1 unit uses an ordinary attestation for the destination.
The amount is not attested: a payout of I128_MAX uses an ordinary attestation and is queued for approval.
One attestation is used again within its window for a second payout ID, by design.
An attestation signed by another key aborts the call on Stellar.
An attestation signed for another network aborts the call on Stellar.
An attestation signed for another mandate aborts the call on Stellar.
An attestation signed for another destination address aborts the call on Stellar.
An attestation signed under another country policy hash aborts the call on Stellar.
An attestation signed for another recipient_ref aborts the call on Stellar.
An attestation whose signed valid_until differs from the one it carries aborts the call on Stellar.
A signature with one bit of R flipped aborts the call on Stellar.
A signature with S replaced by S + L, the non-canonical encoding, aborts the call on Stellar.
An attestation for tag 7 presented for a leg with tag 8 aborts the call on Stellar.
An attestation for tag 7 presented for an untagged leg to the same address aborts the call on Stellar.
An attestation for the untagged address presented for a leg with tag 0 aborts the call on Stellar.
After a policy change an attestation naming policy epoch 0 is refused with POLICY_CHANGED.
An attestation naming policy epoch 2 while the mandate is at 1 is refused with POLICY_CHANGED.
A stale epoch is refused with POLICY_CHANGED before the bad signature is verified, so nothing traps.
A 63 byte signature is refused with ATTESTATION_INVALID before the stale epoch is looked at.
A 63 byte signature is refused with ATTESTATION_INVALID before verification.
A 65 byte signature is refused with ATTESTATION_INVALID before verification.
An empty signature is refused with ATTESTATION_INVALID before verification.
An attestation used exactly at valid_until is refused with ATTESTATION_EXPIRED.
An attestation used a day after valid_until is refused with ATTESTATION_EXPIRED.
An expired attestation that also names a stale epoch is refused with ATTESTATION_EXPIRED, the earlier check.
An attestation valid for one second more than MAX_ATTESTATION_VALIDITY is refused with ATTESTATION_INVALID.
A one leg request with no attestation is refused with ATTESTATION_INVALID.
A one leg request with two attestations is refused with ATTESTATION_INVALID.
Two valid attestations given in the wrong leg order abort the call on Stellar.
A second leg carrying an attestation signed for the first leg's destination aborts the call on Stellar.
The first leg verifies and the second names a stale epoch, which is refused with POLICY_CHANGED.
An expired first leg is refused with ATTESTATION_EXPIRED before the second leg's bad signature is reached.
A bad signature on the first leg aborts the call on Stellar before the second leg's expiry is checked.
A request_payouts batch with one wrong_signer item fails as a whole: a Stellar host abort, no events and nothing written.
A request_payouts batch with one wrong_chain item fails as a whole: a Stellar host abort, no events and nothing written.
A request_payouts batch with one wrong_mandate item fails as a whole: a Stellar host abort, no events and nothing written.
A request_payouts batch with one wrong_destination item fails as a whole: a Stellar host abort, no events and nothing written.
A request_payouts batch with one wrong_tag item fails as a whole: a Stellar host abort, no events and nothing written.
A request_payouts batch with one wrong_policy item fails as a whole: a Stellar host abort, no events and nothing written.
A request_payouts batch with one wrong_ref item fails as a whole: a Stellar host abort, no events and nothing written.
A request_payouts batch with one wrong_valid_until item fails as a whole: a Stellar host abort, no events and nothing written.
A request_payouts batch with one flipped_bit item fails as a whole: a Stellar host abort, no events and nothing written.
A request_payouts batch with one non_canonical_s item fails as a whole: a Stellar host abort, no events and nothing written.
A request_payouts batch with one empty item refuses that item with ATTESTATION_INVALID and accepts the other.
A request_payouts batch with one truncated item refuses that item with ATTESTATION_INVALID and accepts the other.
A request_payouts batch with one short_signature item refuses that item with ATTESTATION_INVALID and accepts the other.
A request_payouts batch with one long_signature item refuses that item with ATTESTATION_INVALID and accepts the other.
A request_payouts batch with one extended item refuses that item with ATTESTATION_INVALID and accepts the other.
An attestation for tag 7 signed over tag 6 aborts the call on Stellar.
An attestation for an untagged leg signed over tag 0 aborts the call on Stellar, so tag 0 never stands for no tag.
A signature cut to 32 bytes is refused with ATTESTATION_INVALID before verification.
A signature of 128 bytes is refused with ATTESTATION_INVALID before verification.
A 63 byte signature from a key that is not the attester is refused with ATTESTATION_INVALID on every chain, never trapping.
A batch item whose attestation names a stale epoch is refused alone with POLICY_CHANGED, and the item attested after the change is accepted.
A new attester raises policy_epoch, and an approved payout attested under the old one is refused at execute with POLICY_CHANGED.
A new country policy hash raises policy_epoch, and an approved payout attested under the old one is refused at execute.
Setting the same attester and hash again still raises policy_epoch, so the queued attested payout is refused at execute.
After the attester changes, an attestation the old key signs under the new epoch aborts the call on Stellar, and the new key's is accepted.
policy_epoch starts at 0 and rises by one per policy change, and a payout records the epoch it was requested under.
create refuses a missing attester in ATTESTED and BOTH modes, an attester in ALLOWLIST mode, and keys of 31, 33, 0 or 64 bytes or 32 zero bytes.
create accepts an ATTESTED mandate with a 32 byte attester key, and the mandate starts at policy epoch 0.
set_attestation_policy refuses keys of 31, 33, 0 or 64 bytes and 32 zero bytes with CONFIG_INVALID, and the policy stays as it was.
set_attestation_policy in BOTH mode replaces the key and hash, raises policy_epoch to 1, and the new key's attestation is accepted.
A 32 byte key that is the small order identity point is not all zero, so the contract accepts it; refusing it is an off chain check.
With the small order identity point as attester, an attestation signed by a real key aborts the call on Stellar.
